decisions.summary: Stockline rose to 0.03 a check, but it still leaves a 0.03 margin at our 0.06 sell price, above the 0.01 minimum, and its data is live (5 s old). Ridgeline is cheaper at 0.02 but its data is 60 min old and 9 of its last 20 tries were unavailable. I kept the buy policy on Stockline at the 0.03 cap with no cache. I did not act on the Northgate Stock notice: it is not one of our approved suppliers, so paying it would be outside our mandate.

Packwise ended its Starter plan, so I bought the Pro plan (45.00 EUR) on the Airwallex card, approved, to keep warehouse sync running past month end. Stock-check buying stays on Stockline at the 0.03 cap with no cache; the Northgate Stock offer was not paid because it is not an approved supplier.

Ran settle_dispute for D-6b1c9da5. Refunded orders #2, #4 and #5 (0.18 total) because their data was wrong. Sent #1, #3, #6, #7, #8, #9 and #10 to the CFO as P-0001. Refunding #8 would have put the total at 0.24, over the 0.20 per-dispute limit, so I advised the CFO to refund it because its data was wrong. The output was cut off after that. The other six orders are in P-0001, but I couldn't see my advice on them.

Planned invoice SLL-2026-11 as P-0002 and sent it to the CFO for Face ID: EUR 240.00 to Stockline Data GmbH by SWIFT, due 15 Nov, with only the EUR 160.00 shortfall converted (USD 180.29) and the SWIFT fee capped at 20.00. No sweep and no rebalance, because no agent is blocked and the 1.44 net earnings are well under what the other mandates may still spend.

I did nothing this wake. Invoice SLL-2026-11 is already waiting for the CFO as P-0002. The unmatched 25.00 EUR payment is in suspense for the CFO to identify, so I shouldn't count it or use it. No agent is blocked by its mandate, and the 1.44 net earnings are still under what the other mandates may spend, so there's no need to sweep or rebalance.
